items.problem: The skill tells the agent to 'confirm each scenario actually renders (controls present, not an empty page)' after launch, but gives no reliable way to distinguish a *painted* page from a *laid-out-but-blank* page. The agent's only in-loop signal is the UIA tree, which was fully populated (all controls present with real coordinates) even though the window painted pure white — so the guidance was satisfied yet the app was blank.
items.evidence: SKILL.md ~132 and ~160 ('navigate to every migrated scenario ... confirm its content frame actually renders (controls present, not an empty page)'). UIA ui/01.json shows all controls present with layout coords; parity screenshots are uniform white. The agent declared done with validator PASS.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md Step 3 note (~line 132) and Step 4 check #7 note (~line 160): 'Verify each scenario renders yourself'; MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#silent-navigation-failures.
items.proposed_improvement: Sharpen the existing 'confirm it renders' wording to warn that 'controls present in the UIA tree' does NOT prove the page paints — a fully populated UIA/visual tree can still render blank white when composition-dependent window chrome (backdrop, extend-into-titlebar/TitleBar) fails to present. Point the reader to the broadened blank-window section and instruct proactively minimizing composition-dependent scaffold chrome rather than relying on a visual check the agent cannot perform headlessly.
items.generalizes: Any migrated app can populate its UIA tree and still paint blank in the automated-capture environment; clarifying that UIA-present != pixels-painted, and steering toward reliably-composited default chrome, helps every scenario, not just LampArray.
